cards.subject: The Most Holy Trinity enthroned in heaven, composed for the arched window. God the Father (left) and God the Son (right) seated side by side on a long bank of golden cloud, both half-length, turned slightly toward each other: the Father in a white robe and a golden-yellow mantle, his right hand raised in blessing, his left resting on a clear crystal globe of the world topped by a small gold cross; the Son in his rose-red tunic and blue mantle, bare-footed, the wounds only as small clean marks on his hands, holding a plain upright wooden cross in the crook of his left arm and raising his right hand in blessing. Between their heads and a little above them, the white dove of the Holy Spirit with outspread wings in a radiant burst of golden light, rays falling on both. Around them, small child-angels' heads among the clouds and a deep blue sky scattered with gold stars at the top of the arch. No lettering anywhere; keep the dove, the cloud and both figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: God the Father as in recurring-figures.md: the Ancient of Days, a venerable man of about seventy with a BROAD, SQUARE-BROWED face — a wide, smooth forehead, a strong straight nose, deep-set, kindly grey-blue eyes under full white brows, broad cheekbones, a calm mouth half hidden by the moustache; snow-white hair falling in soft waves to the shoulders and a long, full, flowing white beard; a triangular gold halo; he sits at the left. Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo ringed with rays; he sits at the right. The two must read as clearly different: the Father old, white-haired and white-bearded with a broad square brow; the Son young, chestnut-haired, with a long oval face.
cards.basis: The Father and the Son enthroned side by side with the dove between them is the common Western image of the Trinity in the Baroque (Ribera's and Guido Reni's Trinities, the Coronation altarpieces); the Father's aged form follows the Ancient of Days of Daniel 7:9. Christ keeps the set's face from transfiguration.

sources.title: Daniel 7:9 (Douay-Rheims), the Ancient of Days
Wikipedia: Trinity in Christian art

cards.subject: The Corpus Christi procession passing through the narrow street of a small hill town at mid-morning, composed for the arched window. In the centre, a priest seen in profile, in a white-and-gold cope with a white humeral veil over his shoulders, holds up a golden sunburst monstrance with the white Host at its heart, plain and unmarked; above him four men carry a white-and-gold canopy on poles. Before him two small altar servers in red cassocks and white surplices swing a censer and carry tall candles, and a little girl in white scatters rose petals. The cobbled street is laid with a carpet of flower petals in simple geometric patterns (no lettering); townsfolk kneel at both sides, a mother with a child, an old man with his hat in his hands. Behind, whitewashed houses with hanging tapestries at the windows and a bell tower against a clear blue sky. The monstrance, bright with light, is the focus. Figures small and serene; no lettering anywhere, no symbols or letters on the Host, the canopy or the tapestries.
cards.face: The figures are small and secondary: the priest, about fifty, a lean, LONG face with a high forehead and a straight nose, clean-shaven, short grey hair, seen in profile with eyes on the Host; the servers, two boys of about ten, one round-faced and dark, one freckled and fair; the flower girl, about seven, dark braids; the kneeling mother with a broad, warm face under a light scarf; the old man with a narrow, bony face and white stubble.
cards.basis: The Eucharistic procession with the monstrance under a canopy and a carpet of petals is the feast's own public act since the fourteenth century (the flower carpets of Brazil and Italy are still laid). No principal face.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Feast of Corpus Christi
Wikipedia: Monstrance

cards.subject: Christ half-length, facing the viewer, in a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle, his left hand gently drawing the mantle aside and his right hand pointing to his Heart, shown on his breast above the tunic: a radiant heart surrounded by a small crown of thorns, a little flame and a small cross rising from its top, golden rays streaming from it; a small, clean mark on it, no blood. The wounds on his hands show only as small, clean marks. His gaze meets the viewer with tender invitation. Behind him, through a soft golden light, the quiet chapel of the Visitation convent at Paray-le-Monial in Burgundy, its round-arched stone nave and the grille of the nuns' choir, candles on the altar. No lettering anywhere.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; he looks straight out at the viewer with a gentle, inviting gaze.
cards.basis: The image follows St. Margaret Mary Alacoque's description of the 1673–75 revelations at Paray-le-Monial (the Heart on a throne of flames, crowned with thorns, surmounted by a cross), as painted in the nineteenth-century devotional type. Christ keeps the set's face.

sources.title: Catholic Encyclopedia (1910): Devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus
Wikipedia: Sacred Heart

cards.subject: Christ the King enthroned in glory, half-length, facing the viewer, composed for the arched window. He wears a white robe embroidered at the neck and hem with gold and a crimson royal mantle lined with gold, clasped at the breast; on his head a simple gold crown set with a few red stones, a plain gold halo ringed with rays behind it. In his right hand, raised, a slender gold sceptre; in his left, held against his knee, a golden orb of the world topped by a cross. The wounds on his hands show only as small, clean marks. He sits on a gold throne on clouds; below the clouds, far off and small, the round blue earth with its seas and lands in soft light, and on either side of the throne a kneeling angel in white with folded wings, adoring. A deep blue sky with gold stars at the top of the arch. No lettering anywhere.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; he looks out at the viewer with calm, serene majesty.
cards.basis: The enthroned, crowned Christ with sceptre and orb is the Pantocrator made royal, the image that spread after Pius XI instituted the feast in 1925 (Quas primas). Christ keeps the set's face, in glory colours with a king's mantle.

sources.title: Pius XI, Quas primas (1925)
Wikipedia: Christ the King

cards.subject: The grotto of Massabielle at Lourdes, 1858, composed for the arched window. High in the rock, in the small oval niche above the grotto's dark mouth, Our Lady stands small and luminous in a soft golden light: a plain white dress falling to her feet, a long white veil over head and shoulders, a sky-blue sash at the waist with its two ends hanging down in front, a golden-yellow rose on each bare foot, her hands joined at the breast, a rosary of white beads on a gold chain hanging from her arm; her eyes lowered kindly toward the girl. A wild rose bush (eglantine) grows from the rock beneath the niche, and ivy trails down the grey stone. In the foreground, half-length at the lower left, Bernadette kneels in three-quarter view, looking up, hands joined around her rosary: a white capulet (the Bigourdan hood) over her head and shoulders, a dark wool dress, a small brown shawl. At the right, the clear waters of the river Gave, poplars and a winter sky. No lettering anywhere.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under the long white veil of the apparition, about sixteen as Bernadette saw her, smiling faintly. Bernadette, clearly different and earthier: a girl of fourteen, small and slight, with a SOFT OVAL face a little broad across the cheekbones — a smooth, rather high forehead, strong, straight, dark brows nearly level, large dark-brown eyes set wide apart, a straight nose with a slightly broad, rounded tip, full lips in a small closed mouth, a softly rounded chin; olive, sun-browned skin; very dark brown hair, centre-parted and drawn back under the capulet; her gaze lifted, rapt and simple.
cards.basis: The Lady's dress follows Bernadette's own account (white dress, blue sash, white veil, a yellow rose on each foot, a rosary of white beads with a chain of the same colour as the roses); Bernadette's face comes from the Billard-Perrin and Dufour photographs of 1861–63, softened to fourteen.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons: Bernadette Soubirous en 1863, photo Billard-Perrin
Wikipedia: Our Lady of Lourdes (Bernadette's description)

cards.subject: The vision of the scapular, composed for the arched window. At the upper left Our Lady appears on a bank of golden cloud, half-length, in the Carmelite colours: a brown gown, a white mantle drawn over her head above a white veil, a small gold crown; she holds the Christ Child on her left arm and with her right hand holds out a brown scapular, two small plain rectangles of brown wool joined by cords (no lettering, no emblem). The Child, in a white shift, leans toward the friar and blesses him. At the lower right, half-length, St. Simon Stock kneels in three-quarter view, arms opened in wonder to receive it: the brown Carmelite habit with its brown scapular and a white mantle over the shoulders, a hood fallen back. Behind him, the grey stone cloister and chapel of an English medieval friary beside a quiet river at Aylesford in Kent, green meadows and oaks under a summer sky. No lettering anywhere.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white veil and white mantle, a small gold crown; she looks down at the friar with tender gravity. the Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md, about two: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls; a plain gold halo. St. Simon Stock, clearly different: an Englishman of about seventy, clean-shaven, with a gaunt TRIANGULAR face — broad temples narrowing to a small pointed chin, hollow cheeks, a long, thin, slightly aquiline nose, deep-set pale blue eyes lifted in wonder under sparse white brows, a thin-lipped mouth slightly open; white hair in a narrow ring around a wide tonsure.
cards.basis: Carmelite tradition (first written in the late fourteenth century) places Our Lady's gift of the scapular to the prior general Simon Stock in England, commonly at Aylesford, on 16 July 1251; painters (Pietro Novelli, Tiepolo at the Scuola dei Carmini) show her with the Child handing it down to the kneeling friar. His face is a free, distinct invention; no portrait exists.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Simon Stock
Historic England: Shrine of Our Lady of Mount Carmel and St Simon Stock, Aylesford

cards.subject: The miracle of the snow on the Esquiline hill in Rome, a summer night of August turning to dawn, after Masolino's panel. Above, in a round golden glory on a bank of cloud, Our Lady half-length in her blue mantle lets snow fall from her open hands; soft white flakes drift down through a warm summer sky. Below, on the green hilltop among umbrella pines, cypresses and the ruined brick walls of ancient Rome, a patch of fresh white snow lies on the summer grass in the shape of a church's ground plan. In the left foreground, half-length, Pope Liberius in a deep crimson cope with a gold border over a white alb and a white papal tiara bends to trace the outline in the snow with a long-handled hoe; at the right, the Roman patrician John and his wife kneel in wonder in rich dark-blue and rose robes. No lettering anywhere; keep the glory, the snow and all figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white inner veil and blue mantle drawn over the head; small, above, looking down with a gentle smile. Pope Liberius: about sixty-five, clean-shaven, with a BROAD, SQUARE face and a heavy, strong jaw — a low, wide brow, a short, blunt nose, small, wide-set grey eyes under straight grey brows, full cheeks, a firm, wide mouth; short white hair beneath the tiara; eyes down on the snow, absorbed. The patrician John: about fifty, a LONG, NARROW face with a high forehead, a long nose, dark eyes, a short, neat black beard; his wife: about forty-five, a ROUND face with plump cheeks and a small mouth under a white veil, hands joined.
cards.basis: The legend of the snow of 5 August (Liberius, the patrician John and his wife, the plan traced in the snow) as painted by Masolino in the Santa Maria Maggiore altarpiece (c. 1428, Capodimonte), where Liberius is an elderly clean-shaven pope in cope and tiara; here Our Lady alone in the glory lets fall the snow.

cards.subject: The Coronation of Our Lady in heaven, composed for the arched window. Christ (right), seated on a throne of golden cloud, half-length, in a white robe and a blue mantle, lifts a gold crown set with small stars and holds it over the head of Our Lady (left), who kneels beside him on the cloud with her head bowed and her hands crossed on her breast, in a white gown woven with gold and a blue mantle over a white veil. Above them the white dove of the Holy Spirit with outspread wings in a burst of golden light. Around them small angels in white and rose play lutes and a portative organ among the clouds; the whole heaven glows gold, with a deep blue band of stars at the top of the arch. No lettering anywhere.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, matured to about forty-eight (the same woman, not a different face): a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks now a little thinner, faint lines at the eyes, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white veil and blue mantle; she kneels humbly with eyes lowered. Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo ringed with rays; he looks at his Mother with tender love.
cards.basis: The Coronation of the Virgin by her Son with the dove above (Fra Angelico, Lippi and the Gothic tympana) is the traditional image of Mary's queenship, the fifth Glorious mystery, which this card also serves. Both faces follow recurring-figures.md, Our Lady matured as on assumption.

sources.title: Pius XII, Ad caeli Reginam (1954)

cards.subject: Our Lady, Star of the Sea: at dusk over a rough, dark-green sea, Our Lady appears half-length above the waves on a soft bank of cloud, in a white gown and a deep blue mantle drawn over a white veil, her hands open and lowered in protection; directly above her head a single bright eight-pointed gold star shines, its light spreading across the clouds and the water. Below at the right, small, a wooden sailing ship with patched sails rides the swell, its sailors turned toward her, one raising his arms; at the far left, on a rocky headland, a small white chapel and a lighthouse. The storm clouds break to a clear violet sky around the star. No lettering, no monogram anywhere.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white inner veil and blue mantle drawn over the head; she looks down toward the ship with a calm, protective gaze.
cards.basis: St. Jerome's reading of her name as stella maris and St. Bernard's homily 'Respice stellam, voca Mariam' (Super Missus est II, 17) give the feast its traditional image: Mary as the star over a stormy sea. It avoids the monogram, and Our Lady keeps the set's face.

sources.title: Catholic Encyclopedia (1910): Feast of the Holy Name of Mary
Wikipedia: Stella Maris (Star of the Sea)

cards.subject: Mater Dolorosa, half-length, facing the viewer in slight three-quarter view, composed for the arched window. Our Lady in a deep violet-blue mantle over a black gown, a white veil framing her face, her hands clasped at her breast; on her breast, over the mantle, a glowing golden heart from which seven slender silver swords fan outward, three on one side and four on the other, their hilts gold; no blood, no wound shown, only the heart shining. A single clear tear on her cheek. Behind her, at dusk, the hill of Calvary with the empty cross, a white linen cloth hanging over its arms, dark against a sky of deep rose and violet; the walls of Jerusalem faint in the distance. No lettering anywhere.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, matured to about forty-eight (the same woman, not a different face): a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks now a little thinner, faint lines at the eyes, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre, under a white veil and violet-blue mantle; her eyes raised a little toward heaven in quiet grief, sorrowful but serene.
cards.basis: The seven swords piercing Mary's heart, from Simeon's prophecy (Luke 2:35) and the Servite devotion of the Seven Sorrows, are the title's own image; the empty cross with the linen recalls the Stabat Mater. Our Lady keeps the set's face, matured.

sources.title: Catholic Encyclopedia (1910): Seven Sorrows of the Blessed Virgin Mary
Wikipedia: Our Lady of Sorrows
